narrative.overview: ProofMe credits work the way films and records credit people: the role beside the name, and beneath them who signs off. Every page is built on one vertical axis. The site alternates two grounds: deep ink is the title card, warm paper is the liner note.
keyCharacteristics: One axis on every page; role left of it, name right of it.
Two grounds, ink and paper, owning whole regions rather than appearing as accents.
One geometric sans for both voices, from the film title-card tradition.
Hairlines between credit groups. Nothing is boxed.
Teal means "you can press this". Green, amber and red mean a status and nothing else.
Digests and transaction references in a mono face, because they are data.

rules.name: The Reserved Colours Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red are never decoration. Each appears only when it is reporting a status, and always with a symbol and the status written in words.

rules.name: The Two Values Rule
rules.body: Any colour that can appear on both grounds has a value for each. Use the bright value on ink and the deep value on paper; never one value on both.

rules.name: The Name Is Largest Rule
rules.body: In any credit, the name or fact is larger than its role, and the contribution is the largest line in its block.

rules.name: The Data Face Rule
rules.body: The mono face is for digests, transaction hashes and account IDs. It is never used to make something look technical.

rules.name: The Nothing Is Boxed Rule
rules.body: Groups are separated by a 1px hairline or by space. Content is not put in bordered or shadowed containers.

dos: Do start headings, paragraphs and actions on the axis.
Do put the actor, role or kind of fact in the left column, and the name or fact on the right.
Do open every page on an ink title card with one heading and one paragraph.
Do say what a status means in words next to it.
Do label sample content as a sample wherever it appears.
Do keep approval and NEAR anchoring visibly separate. A record is shown as anchored only with a confirmed transaction.
donts: Don't put a small label above a heading. A role sits beside its name, never over a headline.
Don't box content in cards, or add shadows, gradients, glass or glow.
Don't use green, amber or red for anything that is not a status.
Don't show a count, score or badge that is not derived from real, currently valid records.
Don't let the page feel like a registry: no seals, stamps, shields or certificate borders.
Don't hide content behind an animation. Motion moves things; it never makes them appear.
